subject: Clarify billing units for long-context bulk ingest and minimum rounding
messages:
From: Elliot Marks <elliot.marks@nova-retail.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nova-retail.com
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bulk ingest pricing — context length and rounding questions

Mateo,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Nova's data team is excited about trying Redwood for product catalog enrichment. Before we commit to a pilot, procurement has a few questions about how we’ll be billed when we push large batches with long contexts: 

- Do you bill on raw tokens or tokenized units after compression/normalization?
- If we batch 10k product descriptions with an average of 3k characters each (≈600 tokens), how does that map to billing units? Is each request counted separately or merged by a context window?
- What rounding/minimum rules should we expect for short vs long calls? For example, if a call is 0.4 of your billing quantum, is it rounded up to 1?

Also attaching a rough monthly ingest estimate and the initial rate card you sent. We’ll need clear examples to show our finance team.

—Elliot
Elliot Marks
Head of Procurement, Nova Retail
Attachment: nova_rate_card_v2.pdf (see sections 2–3)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Marks <elliot.marks@nova-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bulk ingest pricing — context length and rounding questions

Elliot — thanks for the clear list. Below are concrete rules and worked examples so you can share with finance. I’ve kept the explanation at the billing unit (token) level and included how long-context batching interacts with minimums and rounding.

1) Token base and normalization
- Billing is based on tokenized units (our tokenizer). We bill on tokens after any deterministic normalization (whitespace trimming, standard unicode normalization). Compression or client-side dedup doesn’t change tokenization.

2) Request-level aggregation vs conversation/window aggregation
- For bulk ingest using our batch API, each HTTP request is metered independently unless you enable the \"context-join\" option. With context-join enabled, we stitch consecutive items into a rolling context up to your configured max sequence (e.g., 16k tokens) and bill per resulting inference window.

3) Rounding quantum and minimums
- Billing quantum: 1 token unit (we charge per token, no subtoken rounding).
- Minimum per request: there is a soft minimum of 5 token-charges for the hosted API pilot to avoid micro-request noise. This is negotiable for committed contracts.
- Streaming calls: charged by tokens emitted; partial-token emissions are rounded up to the next whole token.

4) Worked examples (approx numbers)
- Your 600-token doc as a single request (no context-join): charged = 600 tokens (subject to the 5-token minimum, which is irrelevant here).
- If you send 10k separate requests each with 600 tokens: total = 10k * 600 tokens billed.
- If you enable context-join and pack 10 docs per window (assuming no overlap) into windows of ~6k tokens: billed tokens = number_of_windows * window_tokens; so 10k docs / 10 per window = 1k windows * 6k tokens = 6,000,000 tokens billed. This reduces per-document overhead but can increase peak inference time.

5) Commit and discount impact
- Minimums and rounding behavior above is default. For committed Reserved/Dedicated customers we can: waive the 5-token soft minimum, apply per-request aggregation rules, and offer a blended token rate for predictable monthly consumption.

6) Invoice examples and reconciliation
- We include token-level line items per route; sample CSV attached (sample-invoice.csv). If you want, we can provide a reconciliation report that maps request IDs -> billed tokens for audit.

Let me know if you want a short table mapping your monthly scenarios to projected tokens and cost; Marissa and Vanessa are cc’d to help run the scenario and propose a pilot discount.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachment: sample-invoice.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Oct 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bulk ingest pricing — context length and rounding questions

Elliot — quick follow-up from a pricing/packaging perspective. If Nova is comfortable with a 6 month pilot and the volumes Mateo outlined (≈6M tokens/month with context-join packing), we can offer the following pilot package: 

- Pilot discount: 25% off hosted token list rates for the first 6 months
- Waive the 5-token soft minimum for API calls associated with the pilot
- Inclusive reconciliation report weekly; up to two bespoke CSV exports per month at no extra cost
- Optional add-on: Dedicated burst capacity during catalog sync windows (+ separate charge)

A few asks to accelerate contracting:
1) We need a committed monthly minimum (for pilot pricing) — can you confirm a floor of 3M billable tokens/month?
2) Procurement will want explicit language about rounding/minimums and how we handle contested billed tokens in the SOW. We can draft a short clause.

If these terms look reasonable I’ll escalate to our finance team and produce a draft SOW with the rounding language baked in.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Elliot Marks <elliot.marks@nova-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bulk ingest pricing — context length and rounding questions

Thanks — that structure is helpful. A few notes from procurement: 

- Nova can commit to a 3M token/month floor for the 6 month pilot. We’d like the 25% pilot discount to apply to any overage up to 7M tokens/month (i.e., blended discount for the pilot period).
- Please include a short SOW clause that states: \"Billing is measured in whole tokens after Redwood’s standard tokenization. All billed token counts are integers; partial tokens are rounded up to the nearest whole token. The 5-token soft minimum is waived for all API calls that are explicitly part of the pilot as defined in the SOW.\"

If you can send a one-page SOW with that language and the invoice reconciliation cadence I’ll route it to legal and aim to sign the pilot next week.

—Elliot
Elliot Marks
Head of Procurement, Nova Retail
